summary:
Lunar Landing Feasibility & Mission Window Planner

Lunar Landing Feasibility & Mission Window Planner is IRIP’s proposed project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the official challenge Lunar Landing Site Navigator.

It is a web-based platform designed to assess lunar landing feasibility by integrating NASA lunar datasets, solar illumination, terrain elevation, temperature estimates and Earth-communication visibility.

Its key features include:
1. Interactive 3D Moon Exploration: Visualizes 21 lunar regions using NASA LROC/WAC imagery and LOLA elevation data.
2. Intelligent Landing-Site Selection: Allows users to explore predefined mission sites and select custom coordinates.
3. Solar & Environmental Simulation: Estimates lunar illumination, surface temperature and environmental conditions.
4. Automated Landing-Window Prediction: Calculates potential lunar-morning landing opportunities and remaining daylight.
5. GO/CAUTION/NO-GO Assessment: Provides explainable preliminary landing-feasibility results based on terrain, sunlight and communication constraints.
The technology stack includes HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, Python and NASA APIs.

Impact: Our project aims to simplify preliminary lunar mission planning, support scientific research and help students, researchers and space agencies explore potential lunar landing locations through an interactive decision-support platform.
details:
Project Details – IRIP Moon Landing Navigator

IRIP Moon Landing Navigator is a web-based lunar exploration and mission-planning platform developed by Intersteller Robotics and Innovation Park (IRIP) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of identifying suitable lunar landing locations and predicting feasible landing windows by integrating multiple scientific datasets into one interactive decision-support system.

The platform allows users to explore 21 lunar regions through interactive 3D visualization, examine lunar surface elevation and terrain, select predefined or custom landing coordinates, and analyze solar illumination, estimated surface temperature, remaining daylight and Earth-communication visibility. It processes astronomical and geospatial information to predict potential landing windows and generates an explainable GO/CAUTION/NO-GO feasibility assessment.

The project aims to simplify preliminary lunar mission planning, help researchers compare potential landing sites, improve awareness of environmental and operational constraints, and make lunar science more accessible to students and educators.

Its creative aspect lies in combining traditionally separate scientific datasets, astronomical calculations, terrain visualization and mission-window analysis into a unified interactive platform. Instead of simply displaying lunar maps, IRIP Moon Landing Navigator connects scientific information to practical preliminary mission-planning decisions.

We considered several factors, including solar elevation, lunar illumination, regional slope and elevation, estimated surface temperature, remaining daylight, lunar night conditions and Earth-communication visibility.

Technology used: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js/WebGL, Python, Python HTTP Server/API Proxy, NASA SVS Dial-A-Moon API, NASA LRO/LROC datasets, LOLA elevation data and Diviner-derived temperature estimates.

The project uses publicly accessible NASA datasets and open-source technologies, avoiding mandatory paid API subscriptions. Its future development includes high-resolution terrain analysis, boulder detection, surface hazard assessment and mission-specific lander and rover constraints.
